result.title: Band2Net: Frequency-to-Network Transport Distillation for fMRI-Privileged, EEG-Only Session-Condition Decoding
result.summary: Functional MRI resolves large-scale brain networks but is expensive and stationary, whereas EEG is portable but poorly localised. We treat fMRI as privileged information, available during training and absent at deployment, with EEG and fMRI acquired from the same participants under matched conditions but not simultaneously. Band2Net encodes EEG into five frequency-specific connectivity graphs and fMRI into seven canonical network tokens from a frozen teacher, and solves a balanced entropic transport problem between the two token sets that gives each EEG band its own fMRI target. In subject-grouped cross-validation on the PsiConnect psilocybin data set, Band2Net reaches 0.801 ROC-AUC for EEG-only session-condition decoding, 5.0 AUC points (95% CI 1.8-8.2) above an EEG-only student. Although its margins over a single shared plan, a KL-relaxed plan and label-free network descriptors remain unresolved, secondary comparisons favour band-specific transported targets over logit, global-feature, contrastive and pooled-target distillation, though not after Holm correction.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作把 fMRI 当作仅训练期可用的特权信息，将 EEG 编码为五个频段特异性连接图、fMRI 编码为七个网络 token，通过平衡熵传输为每个频段分配各自的 fMRI 目标，实现仅用 EEG 的会话状态解码并取得约 5 个 AUC 点提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 特权模态蒸馏与「为弱模态分配细粒度传输目标」的做法规格，或可类推到 LVR 中用训练期可得的丰富视觉证据去监督部署时无视觉输入的 latent 状态，涉及视觉旁路与贡献分配，但领域相距较远，需核查其目标分配是否真优于共享方案。
